newsitem.title: USA: U.S. September oil deliveries drop 0.6 percent - API.
newsitem.headline: U.S. September oil deliveries drop 0.6 percent - API.

text.p: U.S. deliveries of petroleum products in September were down 0.6 percent from a year ago, weakened by a 1.3 percent decline in distillate deliveries and a 0.4 percent decline in gasoline deliveries, the American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday.
In its monthly statistics, the API also said distillate stocks ended September at 113.1 million barrels, the lowest level for that time of year in more than 20 years.
It also said oil imports for September were down 7.7 percent from a year ago.
Domestic crude oil production was up 0.7 percent to average 6.46 million bpd compared with September 1995's 6.42 million bpd, the API said.
Total domestic products supplied in September averaged 17.92 million barrels per day, compared with 18.03 million in 1995, the API said.
Distillates deliveries averaged 3.24 million bpd, down from 3.29 from September 1995, and showing a decline from 1995 for just the second time this year.
Gasoline deliveries dropped, year to year, for the second straight month, averaging 7.75 million bpd in September compared with 7.79 million bpd the previous year.
Deliveries of reformulated gasoline in September averaged 2.41 million bpd, up 21 percent from the previous year's 1.99 million bpd.

Deliveries of kerosine jet fuel rose 8.8 percent from a year ago to average 1.63 million bpd compared with 1.50 million, the fourth consecutive month of growth amid an "unprecedented level of commercial air traffic," the API said.
Residual fuel deliveries fell 2.5 percent to average 827,000 bpd, and deliveries of other oils slipped 3.2 percent to average 4.61 million bpd.
In oil supplies, the API said oil imports averaged 9.0 million bpd, down from September 1995's "unusually strong" level of 9.74 million bpd.

Of that, September's crude imports fell to 7.27 million bpd, their lowest level since March and down 9.2 percent from a year ago. Withdrawals from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve made up for part of the reduced crude imports.
Distillate imports rose by about 35,000 bpd from a year ago to average 178,000 bpd in September, but were down slightly from August.

Distillate stocks grew by more than 3 million barrels in September, but still were about 18.6 million barrels lower than last year and about 22 million barrels below the five-year average for September's end.
Total stocks of oils ended September at 974.8 million barrels, up from 972.7 million at the end of August.
